rhind

rhind provides vectors of exact fractions, with the numerator and denominator stored separately as whole numbers.

  • Fractions are displayed as they were written, so 3/10 and 30/100 remain distinct to read.
  • Arithmetic, comparison and summaries are exact, with results in lowest terms.
  • The components are integers or doubles, and integers become doubles when results need larger numbers.

Installation

You can install the development version of fraction from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mitchelloharawild/rhind")

Usage 

library(rhind)

fraction(1, 3) + fraction(1, 6)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 1/2

x <- fraction(c(2, 30), c(4, 100))
x
#> <fraction<double>[2]>
#> [1]    2/4 30/100
frac_simplify(x)
#> <fraction<double>[2]>
#> [1]  1/2 3/10

fraction(2, 4) == fraction(1, 2)
#> [1] TRUE

Whole numbers are fractions, and other numbers give doubles unless converted with as_fraction().

fraction(1, 3) + 1
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 4/3
fraction(1, 3) + 0.5
#> [1] 0.8333333
fraction(1, 3) + as_fraction(0.5)
#> <fraction<double>[1]>
#> [1] 5/6

See vignette("rhind") for details.

Caveats

  • Results needing whole numbers larger than 2^53 are missing, with a warning.
  • c(x, 1) gives doubles, use c(x, 1L) to combine as fractions.
  • fraction vectors are records, so don’t have names or dimensions, and some base functions such as table() and summary() don’t treat them as numbers.
